FAQ
What file do I open?
Open the .schedule file. That is the workbook.
Where is my workbook saved?
On this computer, in the folder you picked when you saved it. In Chrome and Edge the start screen offers to reopen your last workbook. In Safari and Firefox each save downloads a fresh copy instead — keep the newest one and open it with Open .schedule.
I closed without saving — is my work gone?
The app warns you before closing with unsaved changes. In Chrome and Edge, once a workbook has been saved to a .schedule file, later edits save to that file automatically. In Safari and Firefox there is no auto-save — use Save .schedule, watch for Downloaded in the toolbar, and keep the newest download (the file you opened is not changed).
Is my data private?
DaySchedule does not transmit your schedule. The app works offline and its Content Security Policy blocks application network requests. Files in a synced or shared folder follow that folder’s settings. An embedded app also depends on the hosting site and its administrator.
Can I open an older export (scheduledata.js)?
Yes — use Open .schedule and pick the .js or .json file. It opens as a workbook you can then save as a .schedule file.
Can multiple people edit?
Safest answer: one person edits the workbook file at a time.
Audience vs Specific People?
Audience is the group. Specific People is for named people.
Where do I change the look?
Use Customize.
Where is Save?
Use Save .schedule in the bar under the toolbar, or open the … menu (top right). Once a file is attached the bar button reads Save Now.
When should I save?
Save the .schedule file before closing or handing it off.
